narrative: Material PL1__ME16AB86 shows intermittent demand with only 48.6% non-zero working days and a high CV of 1.35, classifying it as compound-Poisson. Lead times are moderately variable (CV 0.37), clustering bimodally around 2 and 4 working days. Demand variance dominates buffer sizing (82.5% of sigma_LTD), requiring a safety stock of 416 units — far above the current SAP setting of 69. The EOQ of 816 units reduces annual ordering events from ~116 to ~31, cutting total inventory cost by 27.2% while remaining well within the 1,891-unit storage cap.
warnings: Low demand frequency (48.6%) — intermittent regime; periodic review policy recommended
Safety stock increase of +503% vs. current SAP — phase implementation to manage working capital

research_insights.selection_rationale: Despite intermittent demand, the (r,Q) policy is appropriate here because demand volumes on active days are substantial (mean 210 units on non-zero days) and lead times are short enough that a fixed reorder point provides adequate protection. The EOQ balances the high ordering cost against holding cost efficiently.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap is non-binding (65.1% utilisation at peak). No capacity-driven service degradation expected.
